title: Nine Lines of Signing
subtitle: 证书与文凭 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 证书与文凭（生活与学习·学业与证书）
meta: 主题语境：证书与文凭（生活与学习·学业与证书）　|　核心词汇：certificate　|　正文 335 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 certificate 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1957 my mother was sent to sign ① certificate she could not read, and she said the signing was the whole of the lesson. The ② certificate, meaning the paper and not the qualification, was nine lines long and was signed by whoever came last; certificate, she said, is the only thing in an office that is judged by how much has been taken out of it.

Every ③ certificate in that office had the same seal, and the ④ certificate at the end, meaning the one the registrar kept and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever signed properly. Certificate, my grandmother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to stay behind; my mother said the patience is the part that gets everywhere.

My father meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ certificate was the whole of the school, meaning the qualification it carried and not the paper. The ⑥ certificate, meaning the qualification and not any of that, is the only thing in a school that everybody wants and nobody questions; certificate, he said, is either something you sign or the only word that means both a paper and a qualification. She said the qualification is the part they remember.

By 1970 the ⑦ certificate had become a number in a report, and the report had become an argument about the seal. The ⑧ certificate of the whole thing, my mother wrote in April, was nine lines and eleven years of signing; certificate, she said, is either the one at the end or the reason you learned to stand on a chair. He said the chair was never mentioned.

The ⑨ certificate I remember is the one at the end, which was signed in 1975 and is still described as the oldest in the county. A ⑩ certificate, my grandmother said in 1980, is the only thing that improves by being signed; every certificate, she said, is a qualification that has agreed to look like a paper. She said the qualification was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: B. n. 证书（指那张纸本身，与那份资格相对）
C. 固定搭配：sign a certificate 签署一份证书
D. n. 证书（指办公室里每一份）
E. n. 证书（指末尾那一份）
F. n. 资格（抽象：它承载的那份资格）
G. n. 那份资格（抽象：那件事本身）
H. n. 权衡；整件事的分量（抽象总称）

items.q: The certificate, meaning the paper and not the qualification
certificate was the whole of the school
the certificate had become a number in a report
The certificate of the whole thing
A certificate, my grandmother said in 1980

answers.why: sign a certificate 意为“签署一份证书”，1957 年母亲被派去签署她读不懂的那份证书。
certificate 意为“证书、文凭”，指那张纸本身而不是那份资格，共九行，由最后来的人签署。
certificate 指办公室里每一份证书，每一份都是同样的印章。
certificate 指末尾那一份（注册主任保留的那一份），是唯一有人认真签署过的。
certificate 意为“资格”，抽象指它承载的那份资格，父亲说 certificate 就是那所学校的全部。
certificate 为抽象用法，指那份资格本身，是一所学校里人人都想要、却没人质疑的东西。
certificate 意为“证书、文凭”，到 1970 年这份 certificate 成了报告里的一个数字。
certificate 意为“权衡、整件事的分量”，母亲四月写道，整件事权衡下来是九行字和十一年的签署。
certificate 意为“证书”，我记得的是末尾那一份，1975 年签署，至今仍被说成全县最老的。
certificate 为抽象总称，祖母说一份证书是唯一会因为被认真签署而变好的东西。
